note: The input ELF section named .BTF.ext is accepted as attacker-controlled btf_ext_data for later parsing.
The raw bytes and size of the input-controlled .BTF.ext section are passed into the BTF extension parser.
The .BTF.ext candidate bytes are copied into btf_ext->data; the malicious header fields remain input-controlled.

The parser adds the input-controlled subsection offset to the header pointer without first requiring ext_sec->off to be within data_size - hdr_len, allowing pointer wraparound or an out-of-section pointer.
The bounds check is performed after the unchecked pointer addition, so an overflowing info pointer can evade the intended end-of-section check.
The parser reads the record size through the malformed info pointer, producing an out-of-bounds read outside the .BTF.ext allocation.
